topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session by framing how known cellular and molecular components will be integrated to explain the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Innate recognition via PAMPs, DAMPs, and pattern recognition receptors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the innate immune system senses microbial presence and tissue damage through conserved molecular patterns, receptor localization, and downstream signaling complexes.

topics.label: Sentinel cell activation, leukocyte recruitment, and systemic inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how sentinel cells initiate local leukocyte recruitment into tissues, drain fluids toward lymph nodes, and potentially trigger dangerous systemic inflammatory responses.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic adaptations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address how acute inflammation is actively and passively terminated, how damaged tissue is repaired, and how persistent stimuli lead to chronic inflammation and granuloma formation.
